key_terms: The delivery claim for a whole Kafka to Flink to Pinot path, which holds only if every source, checkpoint, sink and serving boundary supports it.
A stable business identifier for each event, distinct from the Kafka offset that identifies only its log position.
Whether a sink takes part in Flink's checkpoint commit protocol, which is required before output can be called exactly once.
A finite record of event IDs, keys, timestamps and correction semantics used to reconcile results after a restart or retry.

worked_examples.title: Deduplicate by event ID before aggregating
worked_examples.interpretation: The repeated event a stands for a producer retry that Kafka delivered twice. Keyed on event_id, the duplicate is dropped and east stays at 4 instead of 8. Exactly-once settings inside Flink do not remove a duplicate that the producer wrote as two records, so the end-to-end guarantee needs a stable business key somewhere in the path.

worked_examples.title: Consumer offsets as the source position
worked_examples.interpretation: With GROUP_ID set to the Flink consumer group, the output lists each partition with CURRENT-OFFSET, LOG-END-OFFSET and LAG. Flink stores its real source positions in checkpoints and only commits offsets to Kafka for monitoring, so these numbers can trail what a restore would use. Record both the checkpoint ID and the committed offsets in the receipt, and compare serving row IDs against the source range they claim to cover.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
